frontmatter.name: feedback-csharp-comments
frontmatter.description: User wants a summary/comment block on every C# script (uploaded or newly generated) explaining what it is and what it's used for

files.content:
Every C# script — whether the user uploads an existing one or I generate a new one — should get a summary comment describing what the script is and what it's used for.

**Why:** Explicit standing request from the user (2026-08-19) for this Unity project. This overrides the general default of "no comments unless non-obvious" specifically for C# scripts in this project.

**How to apply:**
- When generating a new C# script (via `create_script`, `manage_script`, or Write/Edit on a `.cs` file), add a brief header comment (e.g. an XML `/// <summary>` or a top-of-file block) stating the script's purpose and role (what it's attached to / what system it belongs to).
- When the user uploads/shares an existing C# script that lacks such a summary, add one describing what it does, rather than leaving it uncommented.
- Keep the summary concise — what the class/script is for and how it's used — not a line-by-line narration of the code.

mcpServers.name: UnityMCP
mcpServers.purpose: Bridge to the 'MCP for Unity' Unity Editor package for this project - scene/GameObject/component/script/prefab/camera/console automation (~48 tools).
reauthSteps: Open this Unity project (see git.remote) in Unity Editor on the new machine.
Ensure the 'MCP for Unity' package is installed in the project (check Packages/manifest.json; reinstall from its original source if missing).
Start Unity Editor so the bridge listens on 127.0.0.1:8080 (or its configured port).

Re-register the server in Claude Code for the new project path (old registration is keyed to the old absolute path and will not carry over) - accept the auto-detected local server prompt, or add manually: type=http, url=http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp.
The unity-mcp-skill will re-sync automatically once connected - no manual step.

rebuildChecklist: Install Claude Code on the new machine.
Sign in with jcabaldan@netsolar.com.ph (NetSolar org, team_standard seat) - restores account/org/policy-limits automatically.
git clone https://github.com/cabaldanjehoshaphat/Lakbay-Salita.git; set git user.name=cabaldanJehoshaphat, user.email=cabaldanjehoshaphat@gmail.com.
Open the project folder in Claude Code and accept the trust-project prompt.
Recreate ~/.claude/projects/<new-encoded-path>/memory/MEMORY.md and feedback_csharp_comments.md verbatim from the memory.autoMemory section above.
(Optional) Recreate ~/.claude/settings.json with {"syntaxHighlightingDisabled": false, "theme": "auto"} - also the CLI defaults.
Open the Unity project in Unity Editor with the MCP for Unity package installed.
Start Unity Editor so the bridge listens on http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp.
Let Claude Code detect/register the UnityMCP server for the new project path (or add manually: type=http, url=http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp).
No action needed for unity-mcp-skill - regenerates automatically once connected.
No action needed for plugins - claude-plugins-official auto-installs.
Verify by asking Claude Code what Unity scene is open.

(Optional) Copy the *.jsonl session transcripts + memory/ folder to the new machine's equivalent encoded project folder if you want `claude --resume` history to carry over (only works if the new absolute project path encodes to the same folder name).
Nothing else to migrate: no global CLAUDE.md, no rules, no custom agents, no slash commands, no output styles, no workflows exist in this setup.
